title: The Physics Is the Network: Fast, Training-Free Neural Emulation
abstract: arXiv:2610.20525v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Neural emulation need not require learning a substitute for known physics. We investigate PolyNets that couple a continuous-time neural representation of polynomial dynamics with a simple recurrent network for discrete-time integration. When the governing coefficients are known, the resulting tensor graph requires no training and preserves the prescribed numerical scheme while enabling efficient hardware execution and parallel simulation. Using the one-dimensional Korteweg-de Vries equation, we compare PolyNet with CPU and GPU finite-difference Runge-Kutta solvers and three trained neural models: a state-map emulator, a physics-informed predictor, and a learned-tendency integrator. Analytical soliton solutions provide a reference for amplitude and phase errors across grid resolutions, 10^6 dispersively scaled time steps, ensembles of up to 10^4 trajectories, and varying initial amplitudes. translated_title: 物理即网络：快速、无需训练的神经仿真
translated_abstract: 神经仿真不必通过学习已知物理的替代品来实现。我们研究了PolyNet，它将多项式动力学的连续时间神经表示与用于离散时间积分的简单循环网络相耦合。当控制方程的系数已知时，所得到的张量图无需训练，既保留了规定的数值计算格式，又能实现高效的硬件执行和并行仿真。以一维Korteweg-de Vries方程为例，我们将PolyNet与CPU和GPU上的有限差分Runge-Kutta求解器以及三种经过训练的神经模型进行比较：状态映射仿真器、物理信息预测器和学习趋势积分器。解析孤子解为不同网格分辨率、10^6个色散缩放时间步长、多达10^4条轨迹的集合以及不同初始振幅下的振幅和相位误差提供了参考基准。PolyNet实现了与数值求解器相当的精度
tldr: PolyNet将多项式动力学的神经表示与简单循环网络结合，在已知物理系数的情况下无需训练即可构建张量图，实现高效硬件执行和大规模并行仿真，并在KdV方程求解中达到与数值求解器相当的精度。
en_tdlr: PolyNet couples continuous-time neural representations of polynomial dynamics with simple recurrent networks, enabling training-free neural emulation that preserves numerical schemes and achieves accuracy comparable to numerical solvers when the governing physics is known.
